Background == === History === The [[Local Government Act 1972]] created a two-tier system of metropolitan counties and districts covering [[Greater Manchester]], [[Merseyside]], [[South Yorkshire]], [[Tyne and Wear]], the [[West Midlands (county)|West Midlands]], and [[West Yorkshire]] starting in 1974. Dudley was a district of the West Midlands metropolitan county.{{cite book |title=Local Government in England and Wales: A Guide to the New System |year=1974 |publisher=[[HMSO]] |location=London |isbn=0-11-750847-0 |page=7 }} The [[Local Government Act 1985]] abolished the metropolitan county councils, with metropolitan districts taking on most of their powers as [[metropolitan borough]]s. The [[West Midlands Combined Authority]] was created in 2016 and began electing the [[mayor of the West Midlands]] from 2017, which was given strategic powers covering a region coterminous with the West Midlands metropolitan county.{{cite web|title=CONSTITUTION OF THE WEST MIDLANDS COMBINED AUTHORITY|url=https://www.wmca.org.uk/media/1576/constitution-master-module-2642017.pdf|access-date=4 December 2017}} Dudley Council has variously been under Labour control, Conservative control and [[no overall control]] since it was established. The Conservatives controlled the council from the [[2004 Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council election|2004 election]] until Labour gained control in the [[2012 Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council election|2012 election]]. Labour lost overall control in the [[2016 Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council election|2016 election]] but continued to lead the council until 2017, when the Conservatives led the council, still without a majority. In the [[2021 Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council election|2021 elections]], the Conservatives gained a majority on the council, which they kept in the [[2023 Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council election|2023 election]].{{Cite web |last=Farrington |first=Dayna |title=Full election results from Dudley Council as Conservatives gain power |url=https://www.expressandstar.com/news/politics/elections-west-midlands-mayor-pcc-council-2021/2021/05/07/dudley-councils-election-results--in-full/ |access-date=2022-03-26 |website=www.expressandstar.com |language=en}}{{Cite news |title=Dudley result - Local Elections 2023 |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2023/england/councils/E08000027 |access-date=2024-01-02}} The Conservatives lost control of the council in the [[2024 Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council election|most recent election in 2024]], with no party having an overall majority and Labour and the Conservatives ending up with the same number of seats.{{Cite news |date=2024-05-03 |title="Dudley Council election results in full: Tories lose control as they end up level with Labour" |url=https://www.expressandstar.com/news/local-hubs/dudley/2024/05/03/dudley-council-election-results-as-first-wards-are-announced/ |url-status= |work=Express and Star}} After a week of negotiations between the Conservative and Labour groups, it was announced that the existing Conservative leader, Patrick Harley, would remain leader of the council (and therefore appoint the council's cabinet) while Labour would be in charge of the majority of the council's scrutiny committee chairmanships and the mayoralty.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6pypj4gy7ro|title=Council remains Conservative-led after deal struck|date=15 May 2024|access-date=24 May 2024|first1=Martyn|publisher=[[BBC News]]|last1=Smith}} In 2025, six Labour councillors including former Labour group leader Pete Lowe left the party to form the [[Black Country Party]].{{Cite web |date=2025-05-30 |title=Dudley 'Diggers' form new political party to 'be a voice for the alternative' |url=https://www.dudleynews.co.uk/news/25203846.dudley-diggers-councillors-set-new-black-country-party/ |access-date=2025-06-01 |website=Dudley News |language=en}} === Electoral process === The council elects members in thirds every year except the 4th in a four-year cycle.{{Cite web |title=Composition of Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council |url=http://opencouncildata.co.uk/council.php?c=270&y=0 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240102150918/http://opencouncildata.co.uk/council.php?c=270&y=0 |archive-date=2 Jan 2024 |access-date=2 Jan 2024 |website=Open Councill Data UK}} Due to a boundary review of the wards by the [[Local Government Boundary Commission for England]], all 72 seats to [[Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council]] were up in the previous election in 2024.{{Cite web |title=Local Government Boundary Review
